text:
sara: FYI customer AcmeCorp on Dedicated (VPC + on-prem ingress) reporting streaming sessions that drop mid-response and sometimes return partial duplicate sentences on reconnect. They say it only happens when route goes through corporate proxy stack. Attached minimal logs below. Can someone help triage?

sara: customer timeline: start stream -> gets ~200 tokens -> connection gets ECONNRESET from client side -> client reconnects -> receives last 50 tokens again then 'event: done'. They see duplicate tail. :confused:

sara: root log snippet from our runtime (timestamps truncated):
```
[2026-03-10T15:23:05Z] stream:start session_id=acme-01 tokens_streamed=0
[2026-03-10T15:23:06Z] stream:chunk session_id=acme-01 tokens=80 bytes=6400
[2026-03-10T15:23:08Z] stream:chunk session_id=acme-01 tokens=160 bytes=12800
[2026-03-10T15:23:30Z] network:client_reset session_id=acme-01 reason=reset by peer
[2026-03-10T15:23:31Z] connection:reconnect session_id=acme-02 original_session=acme-01
[2026-03-10T15:23:32Z] stream:chunk session_id=acme-02 tokens=230 bytes=18400
[2026-03-10T15:23:33Z] stream:end session_id=acme-02 status=done
```

sara: Customer tcpdump (on their ingress appliance) shows steady small TLS frames followed by a big delayed flush. They suspect proxy is buffering small chunks then releasing on connection tear-down.

devon: Thanks, looking. A couple of quick asks: can we get the raw SSE payload around the reconnect? Also what proxy versions (F5, BlueCoat, corporate nginx?), and are they terminating TLS at the proxy or passing through?

mike: Customer replied: TLS terminates at corp-proxy (F5), then traffic to our on-prem ingress over HTTP/1.1 plain. They said proxy runs "http-proxy" with corporate middleware that rewrites headers. Important: they confirmed proxy adds `Connection: close` to responses when middleware triggers on big responses.

elaine: Two likely behaviors happening together: (1) proxy buffer/aggregation of small chunked responses until either a threshold or connection close; (2) when client reconnects the client library resends the request and our runtime isn't deduping tokens across sessions for that stream id, so we see overlap. That matches duplicate tail.

ingress-bot: Quick note: Dedicated Private uses on-prem ingress v2.1.4 which forwards SSE with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` by default. If upstream proxy switches to `Connection: close` and buffers, chunk boundaries can be coalesced into a final flush only on close.

devon: Repro steps I recommend to the customer to isolate: run direct-bypass to our ingress (skip corp-proxy) and reproduce. If issue goes away -> proxy is culprit. If can't bypass, try forcing HTTP/1.1 and disabling buffering in proxy. Example curl reproducer we asked them to run from inside their network: 
```
curl -N --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: acme-debug-1" "https://redwood-acme.example/stream?session=debug" > out.sse
```

Note `-N` to disable libcurl buffering. If they see chunks arriving immediately vs delayed, that shows buffering.

mike: We also asked them to run a tcpdump of TLS termination point and posted an excerpt:
```
15:23:05.123 TLS 1500 >  15:23:05.125 TLS 120  (many small TLS records)
15:23:30.999 HTTP  2300 ->  (single big HTTP body flush)
```

elaine: Proposed workaround for customer while we investigate: enable a proxy config that disables response buffering and disables HTTP/1.0 fallbacks. For common gateways:
- nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection '';`
- F5/BigIP: enable streaming iRule or disable buffering in the virtual server properties
- BlueCoat-like appliances: ensure streaming passthrough; disable response body caching for SSE endpoints

devon: Also recommend our runtime add an SSE header that hints proxies to not buffer: `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx honors this). We should add it to Private Dedicated by default for known streaming routes. I'll open a tiny runtime PR.

sara: Customer tried `proxy_buffering off` on nginx and reported immediate improvement (no duplicate tail so far) but their corp proxies (F5) still show buffering. They asked if we can support a websocket fallback — they have an internal channel that allows websockets but blocks streaming SSE.

mike: Websocket fallback is doable: we have an internal websocket proxy that can tunnel streaming responses. Short term advise: client can also use `Range` or resume tokens — but that's more intrusive.

elaine: Action items:
- devon -> open runtime change to add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and set `Connection: keep-alive` semantics for Private streaming routes.
- eng-platform -> document onprem ingress best practices for SSE (example nginx snippet, F5 config).
- support (sara) -> ask customer for F5 config dump and version, and coordinate proxy engineers at AcmeCorp for disabling response buffering on the vserver 

devon: One more note: if proxy is doing body-rewrite (e.g., scanning for DLP) it may buffer until closure. In that case the only reliable fix is disabling scanning for the SSE path or using websocket passthrough.

sara: Thanks all. I've told AcmeCorp we have a runtime PR coming and to try websocket passthrough for a fast mitigation. Will update thread with their F5 config when they send it. :thumbsup:

mike: great, ping when you have the F5 dump — also ask them for exact client library versions (some JS EventSource implementations reconnect aggressively, causing overlaps).

elaine: Adding note for postmortem: document how different ingress termination points (TLS at proxy vs TLS passthrough) affect SSE behavior and include checklist for support to triage (bypass test, curl -N, tcpdump snippet, proxy config flags).
